slides.teacher_cue: New pattern — r-controlled vowel ar. When a vowel is followed by r, the r changes the vowel sound. ar makes the long /ɑː/ sound — like the sound a doctor asks you to make. Mouth opens wide, tongue low and back, no rounding. car, far, star, farm. The r colours the vowel — it is no longer short /æ/.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /ɑː/ cleanly in ar words and understand that r controls the vowel before it.
slides.correction_move: Model the contrast: cap /æ/ vs car /ɑː/. Students hear the r changing the vowel. Establish: ar = /ɑː/ — one sound, two letters.
slides.observation_note: Watch for Korean learners producing a short /a/ — the /ɑː/ in ar is longer and further back. Also watch for /l/ substitution for /r/ in words like car, star.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the new focus, then connect ar to one strong word from today.

slides.correction_move: Model the focus once, then have students echo and use it in a known word.
slides.observation_note: Listen for whether students can carry the focus from isolation into a real word.

slides.correction_move: Model car orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for long /ɑː/ — not short /æ/. The r is doing work here.
